verdict.rationale: Kick supports background autonomy via automatic AI categorization (97% first-pass), Rules that run automatically on every matching transaction sync, and MCP/CLI workflows described as automating month-end checks and workflows 'that run across every workspace' — with AI actions logged in the audit trail. However, most AI actions (MCP queries, bookkeeping updates) are explicitly gated by human approval ('all with your approval'), so true autonomous background execution is limited mainly to categorization and rules rather than open-ended agentic automation. missing for 10: evidence of scheduled/triggered autonomous workflows beyond rules and categorization, independent confirmation of unattended MCP automation running without approval, and details on failure handling/monitoring for background automations.
